response.text:
I can’t and shouldn’t infer or declare whether your directs’ calendar entries mean they have a health issue or are interviewing elsewhere. Health status and job-seeking are sensitive, private matters — guessing would risk wrong and could violate privacy.

I can help you handle this safely and effectively. Options below: quick, non-intrusive wording you can send plus a prioritization approach for backfill.

1) Short, neutral interpretations (for your planning only — not assertions)
- "infusion" — commonly used for a medical infusion/treatment, but could mean something else.
- "PT" — ambiguous: often “physical therapy,” but could mean “part‑time,” “personal training,” or another abbreviation.
- "coffee w/ recruiter" — commonly indicates a recruiter conversation (possible job search), but not certain.
- "kid pickup" — caregiving responsibility.
- "support group" — often a peer/health support meeting, but could be another group meeting.

2) Quick, privacy-respecting ways to confirm coverage needs
A) One‑line DM to each person (non-intrusive, doesn’t request details):
"Hi [Name] — I see you have '[event name]' on your calendar next month. Do you need coverage for that time (yes/no), and if yes, what level: full coverage, partial, or remote/async OK? No need to share personal details — just whether you want backup. Thanks."

B) Team announcement + short form (good if multiple people):
"Hi team — I’m doing coverage planning for next month. If you have any calendar blocks where you’ll need someone to cover meetings/tasks, please fill this 30‑second form [link] by [date]. You can indicate only the time(s) and whether you need full coverage or can work remotely. No need to explain personal reasons."

Form fields: Name, Date/time(s), Event title (optional), Coverage required: None / Partial / Full / Remote OK, Best backup(s) (optional), Notes (optional).

3) If you can’t get confirmations, a safe prioritization rule-of-thumb
- Prioritize backfill for events that:
  a) Overlap with high-impact meetings or deadlines (client calls, all‑hands, release windows).  
  b) Are longer or recurring (e.g., multi-hour or weekly).  
  c) Have no known alternate owner or backup.  
  d) Were flagged by the person as "needs coverage."
- Triage order: (1) events that break core coverage (client/stakeholder-facing), (2) long/recurring absences, (3) short/personal errands that can be handled asynchronously.
- Avoid assuming health or job-search status — treat each event on operational impact, not presumed cause.

4) Practical next steps I can do for you now
- Draft the one-line DMs personalized to each direct.
- Create a short form (Google Form) and a team announcement.
- Produce a coverage matrix template (who’s out, who covers, contingency notes).

Tell me which you want me to draft (DMs, team announcement + form, or the coverage matrix) and whether you want the messages to be more formal or casual.
